generated_by: GENERATED by tools/man_gen/gen_kintex7_ypcb00338_man_v1.py (ledger #1235). HAND-ASSEMBLED from the sources in `provenance`; no Xilinx chip database was read. Facts are marked measured / quoted / assumed; unknown values are null with the reason. NOT checked against the schematic.

synthesis.tool: yosys synth_xilinx -flatten -abc9 -arch xc7 -> nextpnr-xilinx -> fpga-as (openXC7.mk as pasted by Alan, 19 Oct; older notes used fasm2frames + xc7frames2bit)
synthesis.loader: openFPGALoader -c ft232 (loads into SRAM only; never write the card's flash)
synthesis.source_language: openXC7.mk hands the source files to yosys as plain arguments, so a .v file is read as plain Verilog and a .sv file as SystemVerilog (checked with the project's yosys, 19 Oct). The generated designs use always_comb, so they must be named .sv. The top file is <PROJECT>.v and the rest go in ADDITIONAL_SOURCES.

nowidelut.note: synth_gowin's -nowidelut has no equivalent recorded for synth_xilinx; not tested.

synthesis.timing_rule: Never load a bitstream that failed timing (what damaged the card before, hardware/YPCB_00338_bringup_findings.md).

device.openxc7_part_note: The part string the openXC7 demo and our own blink were built with (ledger #1194, #1197). The older build script fpga/kintex7_bringup/build_k7_blink_v1.sh uses -2. The speed grade has NOT been read from the chip marking; it affects timing only.
device.jtag_idcode_note: Read on the card with `openFPGALoader -c ft232 --detect` on 17 Oct (ledger #1189) and again on 19 Oct; manufacturer 0x049 (Xilinx), part 0x1b, version 2. openFPGALoader has no name for it and stops after printing it; loading through the openXC7 `make program` works.

logic.note: Slices quoted from the datasheet table (DS180) as recorded in fpga/kintex7_bringup/CARRIER_CELL_SIZE_v1.md (read 17 Oct); 298,600 = 74,650 x 4 LUT6 per slice. Flip-flop total not recorded. A LUT6 is NOT a Gowin LUT4 and not an Intel ALM: the fit tool keeps the three units apart and has no measured Xilinx cost table yet.

dsp.note: DSP48E1 count quoted from the same datasheet note. No assembler cell targets these blocks yet, so no primitive is listed (the assembler reads this list, it does not assume it).

bram.note: Block RAM exists on this family; the count was not recorded, so it is left null.

board.name: YZCA-00338-104 (PCB 00338-P1), sold as a PCIe card; set up here as a stand-alone card

CLK.status: Pin from the old board file; the clock demonstrably reaches the fabric (the demo and our own blink run on the card, ledger #1194, #1197). The 50 MHz value is nominal from the board file: the frequency has not been measured.

LED0.status: Pins proven by the openXC7 demo and our own blink running on the card (ledger #1194, #1195, #1197). Polarity is ASSUMED active-high (the blink looks the same either way); the k7_tree4 lamp test (#1234) is designed to show it.

LED1.status: Pins proven by the openXC7 demo and our own blink running on the card (ledger #1194, #1195, #1197). Polarity is ASSUMED active-high (the blink looks the same either way); the k7_tree4 lamp test (#1234) is designed to show it.

LED2.status: Pins proven by the openXC7 demo and our own blink running on the card (ledger #1194, #1195, #1197). Polarity is ASSUMED active-high (the blink looks the same either way); the k7_tree4 lamp test (#1234) is designed to show it.

leds.note: A steady green LED that no design drives was also seen (ledger #1195): probably a power LED. That is why the k7_tree4 kit signals PASS with a blink, not a steady light.

reset.status: from the old board file, NOT used or tested

config.rule: Never write the card's flash from this project's flows: load into SRAM only (a power cycle undoes it).

jtag.note: JTAG lead only to the PC; the card is powered from its own 12 V supply through the riser with the 1x side unplugged (ledger #1189).

board.io_available: Three LEDs and the 50 MHz clock only. No extra header and no UART (Alan, 19 Oct). Readback is therefore LEDs or JTAG. A JTAG readback is a plan only: feasibility NOT verified. Two routes (Alan, 19 Oct: freeze and save, then read the latch states): (1) the design's own freeze/save shifted out through a BSCANE2 user register; (2) the chip's own state capture and configuration readback, which the open-source loader used here does not do.

capabilities.pcie_note: The card has a PCIe edge connector and an earlier XDMA design is archived (fpga/archive/kintex7_xc7k480t); the PCIe pins were NOT re-checked for this MAN and the active line does not use them.

cell_costs.note: No cell has been measured for this device by this project. Whole-design synthesis counts appear in fpga/kintex7_tests/k7_tree4/README.md only once they have been run.
